acceptance: A worktree created by `make worktree-create`, never pushed, with its tip reachable from the remote and only tool temp files untracked, can be removed through a documented make target with a dry run first.
The same target refuses when the tip has a commit not on the remote or when tracked files are modified, naming the reason.
`.tmp/` DuckDB temp storage left by benchmark runs is either cleaned by the run or ignored by the cleanliness check, with the choice recorded.
description:
Gap. `make worktree-create` is the required way to make any worktree, including throwaway ones (a baseline checkout for timing, a scratch checkout to reproduce a bug). `make worktree-finish` and `make worktree-reap` only remove a worktree whose branch has a merged pull request: for a branch with none they report `HOLD ... No PRs found on GitHub for branch` and `keep`. A worktree with untracked files is held too, even when the files are tool temp output (684 MB of `duckdb_temp_storage_*.tmp` under `.tmp/` in one case on 2026-11-13). The only remaining route is `git worktree remove --force` and deleting the branch ref by hand, which the agent guide classes as destructive commands needing owner approval each time. Such worktrees therefore accumulate.

Expected: a supported removal path for a worktree that was never published: for example `make worktree-finish UNPUBLISHED=1`, allowed only when the branch has no upstream, its tip is reachable from a ref on the remote (so no commit is lost), and untracked files are limited to known tool temp paths or are listed for confirmation.

Guardrails: never remove a worktree holding commits that exist nowhere else, or tracked modifications. Keep the dry-run default and the expected-head check. The evidence contract in `_project/specs/worktree-lifecycle-evidence-contract.md` governs what proof removal needs; extend it, do not bypass it.
